title: 3.9.3 Group PA Part 3: Reflect
description: Part 3 of 3, worth 25%. A short write-up with your partner: who did what, three test cases, one thing you logged, and three Chapter 3 sections found in your code. Grade up to three times; your best try counts.

aiGrader.rubricTitle: Chapter 3 Group PA, reflect third: AI-graded rubric
aiGrader.prompt:
Both partners write this together and each submits it. Everything asked for is something you did in the last hour. Your own everyday words throughout, short is fine.

Part 1 -- Who did what. Name both partners. Then say who drove the keyboard for the plan (3.9.1), who drove it for the code (3.9.2), and one thing the partner who was not typing caught that the one typing had missed.

Part 2 -- Three test cases. The student was told a test case is one run where they know the right answer first, and to give three in a table: what they put in, what they expected, what they got. The program's yes-or-no decision is the subset function (keep an item or leave it out), so at least one of the three must be kept and at least one left out, or the decision was only half tested. Worked examples they were given: Snack Shack with a reorder level of 5 (Pretzel qty 3 is kept, Popcorn qty 12 is left out); Lap Times with a target of 60; Seed Tray with a level of 5; Library Cart with a limit of 300. They were also asked for one line saying whether got matched expected, and what they changed if not. Three cases that all come out the same way do not count, however different the numbers look.

Part 3 -- One thing you logged. Name one console.log you added while building that was there to check your work rather than to report the answer: what you printed, what it showed you, and what you changed because of it (1.5.41). If nothing was wrong, say what the print confirmed and how you would have known if it had been.

Part 4 -- Three sections in your code. Pick any three of the eight Chapter 3 sections: functions and calls (3.1), parameters and return values (3.2), the loop over the array (3.3), the arrow function (3.4), the record objects (3.5), the change the caller can see (3.6), map() (3.7), save and load (3.8). For each, name the function where it appears and quote one line of your own code from it.

rubric.title: Both partners named, with who drove which third
rubric.description: Two names appear, and the response says who had the keyboard for the plan and who had it for the code. Credit generously -- any clear division counts, including 'we swapped every ten minutes' as long as both names are there and both thirds are accounted for. The catch-something-missed detail is a bonus; do not withhold the criterion for a thin one. Withhold only if fewer than two names appear, or if the division of work is not stated at all.

rubric.title: Three test cases, at least one kept and one left out
rubric.description: Three cases are given, each with what went in, what was expected and what the program gave. Credit rough tables, bullet lists or prose equally -- format is not being assessed. The one thing that matters: at least one case is kept by the subset function and at least one is left out, so both answers of the decision are exercised. Credit that if the response makes it visible in any way, including just saying 'this one was not low stock'. If all three land on the same side, mark the criterion partial and say why in the feedback. If fewer than three cases are given, or the expected answer is missing from them, mark it partial at best.

rubric.title: One console.log used to check work, with what it showed
rubric.description: The response names one specific thing they printed while building, what it showed, and what they did next. Credit a print that confirmed something was already right just as fully as one that found a bug -- the response is allowed to say nothing was wrong, as long as it says what the print told them. Withhold only if no specific printed value is named at all, or the answer is generic advice about debugging rather than something that happened.

rubric.title: Three Chapter 3 sections found in the program
rubric.description: The response picks three of the eight Chapter 3 sections (functions and calls 3.1, parameters and return 3.2, the loop 3.3, the arrow function 3.4, the record objects 3.5, the visible mutation 3.6, map 3.7, save and load 3.8) and, for each, names the function where it appears and quotes a line of their own code from it (repeating the section number from the prompt is not enough). Credit when all three are located this way. Partial when two are, or when the sections are named without a function or a quoted line. Missing when none are.
